cases.purpose: Padding through terminal names the candidate's curated table accepts, so an unknown-terminal refusal cannot hide the padding branch. linux flash has mandatory $<200/> padding and no npc: ncurses writes floor(200*38400/9000) = 853 NUL pad bytes at the PTY's 38400 baud, and 213 after 'stty 9600', so padding follows the output speed. vt100 clear carries non-mandatory $<50> (with xon): no pad bytes and no literal '$<50>'. xterm-256color flash has $<100/> with npc: a delay with no pad bytes (timing in migration-tput-padding-npc-delay). The original modes are restored with stty -g.
cases.script:
s=$(/usr/bin/stty -g)
tput -T linux flash; printf 'A\n'
/usr/bin/stty 9600
tput -T linux flash; printf 'B\n'
/usr/bin/stty "$s"
tput -T vt100 clear; printf 'C\n'
tput -T xterm-256color flash; printf 'D\n'

cases.purpose: Padding with npc: xterm-256color flash is \E[?5h$<100/>\E[?5l and the entry has npc, so ncurses flushes the first half, sleeps 100 ms and writes the second half with no pad bytes. padgap.py runs the command on a private PTY it owns, timestamps every byte and records the output bytes and whether >= 80 ms passed between the two halves. Both sides run the same helper; '$BASH -c' is the side's own shell (reference tput from PATH, candidate builtin).

files.padgap.py:
import os, select, signal, subprocess, sys, time
# Runs SHELL -c CMD on a private PTY this helper owns (child stays in this session, ignores SIGHUP) and records
# the output bytes and whether at least 80 ms passed between the end of FIRST and the start of SECOND.
shell, cmd, first, second = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], bytes.fromhex(sys.argv[3]), bytes.fromhex(sys.argv[4])
master, slave = os.openpty()
child = subprocess.Popen([shell, '--noprofile', '--norc', '-c', cmd], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave,
                         close_fds=True, preexec_fn=lambda: signal.signal(signal.SIGHUP, signal.SIG_IGN))
os.close(slave)
data, stamps, deadline = b'', [], time.monotonic() + 8
while time.monotonic() < deadline:
    if select.select([master], [], [], 0.05)[0]:
        try:
            chunk = os.read(master, 4096)
        except OSError:
            chunk = b''
        if not chunk:
            break
        now = time.monotonic()
        data += chunk
        stamps.extend([now] * len(chunk))
os.close(master)
try:
    status = child.wait(timeout=3)
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    child.kill(); status = child.wait()
print('bytes ' + data.hex())
a = data.find(first)
b = data.find(second, a + len(first)) if a >= 0 else -1
if a < 0 or b < 0:
    print('markers-missing')
else:
    gap = stamps[b] - stamps[a + len(first) - 1]
    print('gap>=80ms' if gap >= 0.08 else 'gap<80ms')
print('child-exit %d' % status)

cases.purpose: Special characters after tput reset and tput init. With every special character disabled and erase set to ^H, reset must restore each disabled character to its default and keep erase ^H (ncurses reset_tty_settings replaces only disabled characters). With all of them, erase included, disabled, init restores only erase, intr and kill and leaves the rest disabled (set_control_chars). cc.py records the values on the PTY; the original modes are restored with stty -g after each part.
cases.script:
s=$(/usr/bin/stty -g)
/usr/bin/stty intr undef quit undef kill undef eof undef start undef stop undef susp undef werase undef lnext undef rprnt undef discard undef erase ^H
tput reset; /usr/bin/python3 cc.py reset
/usr/bin/stty "$s"
/usr/bin/stty intr undef quit undef kill undef eof undef start undef stop undef susp undef werase undef lnext undef rprnt undef discard undef erase undef
tput init; /usr/bin/python3 cc.py init
/usr/bin/stty "$s"
printf 'Z-DONE\n'

files.cc.py:
import sys, termios
# Records the special characters of the terminal on stdin: one parity line of values and a summary naming the
# disabled ones (value 0 or _POSIX_VDISABLE, which is 0 on Linux) plus the erase value.
names = [('intr', termios.VINTR), ('quit', termios.VQUIT), ('erase', termios.VERASE), ('kill', termios.VKILL),
         ('eof', termios.VEOF), ('start', termios.VSTART), ('stop', termios.VSTOP), ('susp', termios.VSUSP),
         ('werase', termios.VWERASE), ('lnext', termios.VLNEXT), ('rprnt', termios.VREPRINT),
         ('discard', termios.VDISCARD)]
cc = termios.tcgetattr(0)[6]
val = {n: (c[0] if isinstance(c, bytes) else c) for n, c in ((n, cc[i]) for n, i in names)}
tag = sys.argv[1]
with open(tag + '-cc', 'w') as f:
    f.write(' '.join('%s=%d' % (n, val[n]) for n, _ in names) + '\n')
off = [n for n, _ in names if val[n] == 0]
with open(tag + '-summary', 'w') as f:
    f.write('disabled: %s\n' % (' '.join(off) or 'none'))
    if tag == 'reset':
        f.write('erase=%d\n' % val['erase'])
